| Dimension | Assessment |

| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | *(pending)* |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Interdisciplinary philosophy-of-economics work: methodology, history, and ethics of economics, and economic analysis of philosophical questions. Recent (2025) content includes experimental/behavioral philosophy (dictator-game study of the non-identity problem), philosophy of science applied to economics (mechanistic reductionism in economics), and a running special section on climate justice (loss and damage, adaptation and resilience, beneficiary-pays principle) with 8 peer-reviewed contributions.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** conceptual/philosophical argumentation, history and methodology of economics, experimental/behavioral philosophy (e.g., dictator-game designs), philosophy-of-science analysis of economic theory (e.g., reductionism debates), normative/ethical analysis (e.g., climate justice, distributive justice), critical commentary on previously published articles, archival/historical texts paired with a research article, book reviews and PhD thesis summaries
